:::{#thm-newton-model}
#### The Newton step minimizes the quadratic model

Let $q$ be the quadratic model of $f$ at $\vx$ (@def-quadratic-model),
with $\matr{H} = \matr{H}_f(\vx)$ [positive definite](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite).
Its unique minimizer is the Newton step $\stepvec^* = -\matr{H}^{-1} \vecf{g}$.

:::

::: proof

$\matr{H}$ is symmetric, by the definition of [positive definite](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite),
and invertible ([positive definite inverse](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-pd-inverse)),
so $\stepvec^*$ exists and $\matr{H} \stepvec^* = -\vecf{g}$.
For any $\vecf{d} \in \reals^p$, first

$$
\ba
\tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \stepvec^*
&= -\dprod{\vecf{d}}{\vecf{g}}
&& \text{(} \matr{H} \stepvec^* = -\vecf{g} \text{)}
\\
&= -\dprod{\vecf{g}}{\vecf{d}},
&& \text{(a } 1 \times 1 \text{ matrix equals its transpose)}
\ea
$$

and $\tp{\stepvec^*{}} \matr{H} \vecf{d} = \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \stepvec^*$ in the same way, using $\tp{\matr{H}} = \matr{H}$. Then

$$
\ba
q(\stepvec^* + \vecf{d})
&= f(\vx) + \dprod{\vecf{g}}{(\stepvec^* + \vecf{d})} +\tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{(\stepvec^* + \vecf{d})} \matr{H} (\stepvec^* + \vecf{d})
&& \text{(definition of } q \text{)}
\\
&= f(\vx) + \dprod{\vecf{g}}{\stepvec^*} + \dprod{\vecf{g}}{\vecf{d}}
+ \tfrac{1}{2} \paren{\tp{\stepvec^*{}} \matr{H} \stepvec^* + \tp{\stepvec^*{}} \matr{H} \vecf{d} + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \stepvec^* + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \vecf{d}}
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\
&= f(\vx) + \dprod{\vecf{g}}{\stepvec^*} + \dprod{\vecf{g}}{\vecf{d}}
+ \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\stepvec^*{}} \matr{H} \stepvec^* - \dprod{\vecf{g}}{\vecf{d}} + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \vecf{d}
&& \text{(both cross terms equal } -\dprod{\vecf{g}}{\vecf{d}} \text{)}
\\
&= f(\vx) + \dprod{\vecf{g}}{\stepvec^*} + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\stepvec^*{}} \matr{H} \stepvec^* + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \vecf{d}
&& \text{(cancel } \dprod{\vecf{g}}{\vecf{d}} \text{)}
\\
&= q(\stepvec^*) + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{H} \vecf{d},
&& \text{(definition of } q \text{)}
\ea
$$

which is greater than $q(\stepvec^*)$ for every $\vecf{d} \ne \vzero_{p \times 1}$, since $\matr{H}$ is positive definite.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-newton-model}
#### The Newton step at $x = 2.5$

For the model $q(\step) = f(2.5) + 2.25\,\step + 2.5\,\step^2$ of @exm-quadratic-model,
$H = [5]$ is positive definite, so by @thm-newton-model its minimizer is
$\step^* = -H^{-1} g = -2.25 / 5 = -0.45$.
Setting the derivative $2.25 + 5 \step$ to $0$ gives the same $\step^*$,
and $2.5 - 0.45 = 2.05 = x^{(1)}$ (@exm-newton-method).

:::
